title: Jizmak Da Gusha - Wikipedia
notes: Born Brad Roberts (no date or place given); Gwar's drummer, active 1989 to present; 'Roberts first started playing with Gwar in 1989, after the year's North American tour', after Pete Luchter (Lee Beato) left; credited on Scumdogs of the Universe although a pressing error credited Rob Mosby; X-Cops ('Beat You Down', 'Junkie', replacing Mike Dunn; sings 'Barbells'), RAWG, The Dave Brockie Experience. In-story: a beast from 'The Wide Wide World of Sports', frozen in ice and thawed to replace Nippleus Erectus. Costume: 'somewhat resembles a monstrous dog with very large teeth'; carries a large warhammer; the only character who does not wear full armour on stage, so he can drum; arm coverings with two blades like dragon mouths, a gut-plate and a loin cloth; a wolf-like head with grey fur from War Party (2004), later lupine with brown fur; Roman segmental armour from Violence Has Arrived, later armour of exposed muscle; in behind-the-scenes footage 'he is able to reach all of his cymbals without trouble'. Brad_Roberts_(drummer) redirects here.

title: List of Gwar members - Wikipedia
notes: Drummers: Sean Sumner (1985), Jim Thomson (1985 to 1987 and a 1989 tour; Hans Sphincter, Hans Orifice), Rob Mosby (1987 to 1989; Nippleus Erectus; Hell-O), Pete Luchter (1989, live only; Lee Beato), Brad Roberts (1989 to present; Jizmak da Gusha). Roberts is in the February 2024 to present line-up. Credited from The Next Mutation (1989) and Scumdogs of the Universe (1990) to The New Dark Ages (2022).

title: Gwar - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in Richmond, Virginia, 1984, from Dave Brockie's punk band Death Piggy and Hunter Jackson and Chuck Varga's Slave Pit, the workshop building props and costumes for a film called Scumdogs of the Universe. Genres: thrash metal, heavy metal, crossover thrash, shock rock, comedy. Hell-O a 'crossover thrash metal-punk rock album'. Jim Thompson filled in after Pete Luchter quit in 1989 and 'later quit and was replaced by Brad Roberts'.

title: Scumdogs of the Universe - Wikipedia
notes: Released 8 January 1990, Metal Blade, recorded 1989; produced by Ron Goudie, Hypo Luxa and 'Hermes Pan' (Paul Barker); mixed by Robert Feist at Conway. Heavy metal, crossover thrash, thrash metal, comedy rock. 'Sick of You' the song played most in concert. Personnel: Brockie, Dewey Rowell, Mike Derks, Michael Bishop, Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums. Remixed by Ronan Chris Murphy for the 2020 box set; King Queen 8:09 there.

title: America Must Be Destroyed - Wikipedia
notes: Released 31 March 1992, Metal Blade, recorded 1991, produced by Glen Robinson. Thrash metal, crossover thrash, comedy metal. Tracks include Ham on the Bone, Crack in the Egg, Gor-Gor, Have You Seen Me?, The Road Behind (a power-ballad parody). Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums.

title: This Toilet Earth - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 March 1994, Priority (first pressing) then Metal Blade, produced by Scott Wolfe. Heavy metal, crossover thrash, comedy rock, alternative metal. Opens with Saddam a Go-Go; 'horns appear on the opener'; more cartoonish than earlier albums. Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums. Peter Lee's first album as Flattus Maximus.

title: Violence Has Arrived - Wikipedia
notes: Released 6 November 2001 (planned for 11 September 2001), Metal Blade, produced by Grant Rutledge and Gwar. Thrash metal; 'has more of a thrash metal sound than any of their previous albums' (uncited claim on the page). Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums, percussion. Tracks include Battle Lust, Immortal Corrupter, Beauteous Rot, Biledriver.

title: War Party (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 October 2004, DRT Entertainment, produced by Gwar and Glen Robinson. Thrash metal and heavy metal; 'continues the decidedly heavier focus' of Violence Has Arrived. Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums; Cory Smoot lead guitar, Mike Derks, Todd Evans. Tracks include Bring Back the Bomb, Krosstika, Womb With a View, War Party, Fistful of Teeth.

title: Lust in Space - Wikipedia
notes: Released 18 August 2009, Metal Blade, produced by Cory Smoot and Gwar. Thrash metal, heavy metal, comedy rock. Brad Roberts (Jizmak Da Gusha): drums and percussion. Tracks include Lust in Space, Let Us Slay, Metal Metal Land. Debuted at No. 96 on the Billboard 200, the band's highest debut (Blabbermouth).

title: Drummerszone: Brad "Jizmak Da Gusha" Roberts (artist profile)
notes: Read through a summary of the page. 'At the age of ten, I wanted to quit playing drums, almost as soon as I had started'; his mother's encouragement kept him at it. Besides Buddy Rich: Alex Van Halen, Bill Stevenson, Dave Lombardo, Mikkey Dee, Bill Ward and Billy Cobham; 'You name it, I listened to it.' 'The drummer's job is to make that song swing.' Joined in 1989, replacing Rob Mosby after Hell-O. Endorsements listed: GMS, Evans, Promark, Paiste. Two Grammy nominations, sixteen MTV videos. Dave Brockie eXperience (Diarrhea of a Madman, 2001; Songs for the Wrong, 2003), No Deal (2001), Armstrong (Dallas, 2002, with Zach Blair).

title: 'All Hail Jizmak Da Gusha', maubrecht (blog), 18 August 2017
notes: A fan's essay built on the Drummerszone profile and a CDN interview: the same influences; 'It took four years to get the trap kit and started playing seriously at 14' (CDN); first kit paid for by mowing lawns, his parents matching his savings. Kit: earlier drums painted as distorted eyes or skulls; later mostly unpainted with phrases scribbled on some heads; the whole kit under a large arch on stage. 'The only central GWAR character played by just one person.'

title: Another Rundown (Jarrad James), 'GWAR's Bloodiest Drumset EVER ft. Jizmak Da Gusha', YouTube, 21 November 2025
notes: Filmed in costume at Marathon Music Works, Nashville, on the 40th-anniversary tour; read from the auto-captions and watched (0:00 to 4:00). 1:58 'Yamaha. This is the live oak custom kit, which I happen to wrap in our new comic book, The Return of Gor-Gor', 'a little Prince vibe going with the cymbals, the purple Paiste cymbals'; 2:24 'the kicks are 22 inch kicks, probably 18 inches deep. We got 10in tom, 12in rack tom, and the floors are 14 and 16in floor toms'; 2:37 'a nice 6 and 1/2 in ... Yamaha deep brass snare ... It's got the crack'; 3:00 Evans EC2 on the toms, EMAD on the kick, a reverse-dot hazy EC2 on the snare; 3:28 PST X Swiss cymbals left and right, 15-inch heavy hats, 19-inch heavy crash left, 18-inch crash middle, 20-inch heavy crash, 20-inch heavy ride, 18-inch china; 4:10 a cowbell on the bass drum hoop for 'a couple of old tunes', 10 and 12-inch splashes, a Yamaha pad for an 808 drop; in-ear monitors and a ButtKicker on the throne; 5:17 a backup 'imitation Black Beauty' snare; 6:24 'the first 20 years ... I changed it around all the time ... the last 20 years has probably been the roughly the same setup'; 10:45 ProMark sticks, a signature model ProMark stopped making.

title: Equipboard: Jizmak Da Gusha (Brad Roberts)
notes: Community gear list. Yamaha Live Custom Oak, 'two 22x18 kicks, 10x7 and 12x8 rack toms, two 14x16 floor toms' (as listed); Yamaha Recording Custom brass snare 6.5 x 13 (the rundown says 6 1/2-inch deep, no diameter); Paiste Color Sound 900 cymbals and PST X Swiss; Paiste Rude Shred Bell seen in a 2012 Guelph show; LP Rock Cowbell; GMS drums quoted from DrumMagazine.com ('GMS are the best drums that the humans could come up with'); ProMark 747B nylon-tip Jizmak signature sticks.

title: Paiste: JiZMak Da Gusha (artist page)
notes: Paiste artist since February 1995. Two set-ups, left to right. One: 10" 2002 Mega Bell, 18" PST X Swiss Medium Crash, 14" Color Sound 900 Black Sound Edge Hi-Hat, 19" CS900 Black Heavy Crash, 16" CS900 Black China, 12" CS900 Black Splash, 18" CS900 Black Heavy Crash, 16" CS900 Black China, 20" CS900 Black Ride, 20" CS900 Black Heavy Crash, 12" CS900 Black Splash, 18" PST X Swiss Medium Crash. The other (older, mostly discontinued Alpha): 10" 2002 Mega Bell, 14" Alpha Rock Hats, 18" PST X Swiss Medium Crash, 19" Alpha Rock Crash, 18" Alpha China, 10" Signature Splash, 18" Alpha Medium Crash, 18" Alpha China, 20" 2002 Bell Ride, 20" Alpha Rock Crash, 18" PST X Swiss Medium Crash, 10" Alpha Splash. Bio in character: he 'beats any who cannot keep up with the unrelenting tempo he sets'; precise and forceful. Undated set-ups; the 2025 rundown has purple, not black, Color Sound 900.

title: Spotlight Report, 'Interview: GWAR's Jizmak Da Gusha Promises Chaos in Oz', 14 August 2025
notes: In character, before Good Things Festival (December 2025). 'I just gravitated toward beating things'; 'the only member to have been portrayed by the same human since 1989'; 2025 the band's 40th anniversary; Gwar 'is going to be around forever'.

title: Defenders of the Faith, 'Jizmak Da Gusha (GWAR) Interview', 23 May 2025
notes: Day 3 of Milwaukee Metal Fest. On the 35th anniversary of Scumdogs: a verse of 'King Queen' cut for length, restored on the reissue; he named 'The Salaminizer'; on first hearing King Queen, 'Wow, that's a heavy song that I haven't heard before'. The EP The Return of Gor-Gor, 'fast', 'visceral', with Grodius Maximus's debut.

title: Crash Bang Boom Podcast, '167_Brad Roberts AKA Jizmak Da Gusha-Gwar', 13 January 2020 (episode description)
notes: Only the description was read: The Blood of Gods and two years of touring; the props crew; the difficulty of playing drums in costume; 'a Bad Brains show that changed his life'; the origins of the Jizmak character; Brockie's 1990 arrest. The 44-minute episode itself was not heard.
